//: The tower whose bullwheel is held out by a counterweight. Same sixteen cells as ropeway:pylonbase and the same fifteen offsets as ropeway:drivestation - only the block numbers on the machine leg differ. A line will not carry a cabin until one of its towers is a COMPLETED tension station, which is a structural fact about the chain rather than a distance query, so it is asked by walking line.Towers.
//whytwo: Two station blocks rather than one that is both. On a real aerial ropeway the drive bullwheel is at one end and the return bullwheel rides a tensioned carriage at the other; a combined block would let a player tension the haul rope against the very thing driving it, and there is one leg to spend.
//rope: Cable texture. BuildHalfCable flat-samples ONE point of it - see pylonbase.json. Keep comments OUT of "textures".

attributes.//tensioner: Read once by BEPylonBase.IsTensioner. This one flag is the entire tensioner rule now: a line has its tensioner iff one of its own towers carries it and is complete. There is no matching flag on drivestation.json - a drive station is named by the intake cell it owns, and a second attribute saying the same thing would be a second thing to keep in step.
attributes.//multiblockStructure: The same fifteen offsets as pylonbase.json and drivestation.json, byte for byte. See drivestation.json for why that identity is the point rather than a coincidence. ropeway:layshaft is deliberately the SAME block on both stations: on the drive it is a turning line shaft and here it is a static tie rod, and at 16 pixels those are the same forged bar on the same standards.
attributes.//tensionhead: The -* stays a WILDCARD here and is narrowed at runtime, per tower, by BEPylonBase.OwnTheHeadCell: a north-facing station wants tensionhead-north and an east-facing one tensionhead-east. Writing an exact code here instead would make all four variants demand the same facing. The narrowing is what stops two stations sharing one machine leg - RopewayAssetContractTests.ASharedMachineLegSatisfiesAtMostOneStation fails either way round.
